plan: [ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a (weakly) dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders. Overbidding risks winning and paying more than your value if the second-highest bid exceeds your value. Underbidding risks losing when winning would have been profitable. With value 13 and $0.1 increments allowed, the profit-maximizing bid is exactly 13. This remains optimal even considering others’ rationality and beliefs, because the payment equals the second-highest bid, not your own. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values and rational opponents. The dominant strategy is to bid truthfully: bidding above 15 risks negative payoff if the second-highest bid lies between 15 and the overbid; bidding below 15 risks losing profitable wins when the second-highest bid is below 15. With no informative history and one round, there’s no benefit to reputation or signaling. Therefore, bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With value 47, bidding 47 ensures we win whenever the second-highest value is below 47 and pay that second-highest bid, yielding nonnegative surplus, while avoiding overpay risk. Discreteness (0.1 steps) and random tie-breaking don’t change optimality. With only 1 round, no need to learn; prioritize truth-telling to maximize expected profit. ]
